claims.proposition: RBG PAC spent roughly $20M supporting Donald Trump in late October 2024, including digital advertising targeted substantially at women in swing states.
The ad identified RBG PAC as payer and used Ruth Bader Ginsburg branding/positioning.
May Mailman was the principal publicly visible individual associated with RBG PAC before donor disclosure.
The applicable FEC reporting schedule allowed late-cycle funding to remain undisclosed until a post-election filing.
Post-election filings identified the Elon Musk Revocable Trust as the source of the RBG PAC funding.
Approximately $20.5M from the Elon Musk Revocable Trust funded RBG PAC's late-cycle operation.
Musk's total 2024-cycle political spending was roughly $290M and placed him at or near the top of individual political contributors.
U.S. election spending reached approximately $15B while broad public opinion favors limits/reduced large-donor influence.
The legal-policy dispute turns partly on anti-corruption interests versus First Amendment protection for political spending.

promotion_rule: No source claim promotes to ERL finding until its required primary/authoritative evidence is reconstructed, contradiction-tested, and reviewed under the existing fund-governance lane.
